caption: The drawing depicts a group of figures in a scene dominated by a central horizontal wooden cross, to which a male figure with a crown of thorns is being nailed. The central figure, wearing only a white loincloth, has arms outstretched and legs overlapping, indicating that he is being crucified; his skin is rendered with flesh tones and he is marked with what appear to be wounds or blood. Surrounding him, several figures are dressed in various colors—predominantly reds, browns, blues, and greens. Two figures, one on each end of the cross, appear to be soldiers or executioners. The figure on the left, dressed in yellow and blue with a helmet, is kneeling and stretching the arm of the central figure, while the one on the right in red and green is pulling a rope attached to the other arm. Another standing figure in blue hammers the central figure’s hand to the cross with a large spike. In the background, a group of people stand closely together, some with hands raised to their faces or clasped in front of them, and they wear earth-toned robes. The ground is a mix of green, brown, and yellow, with indistinct patches suggesting grass and dirt. The background also consists of blended earth tones and muted colors, with no specific landscape details visible. The top of the drawing contains handwritten text that reads “Jesus is nailed to the Cross No.11,” and the lower right corner contains the handwritten name “Geoffrey Holt.” The medium is watercolor, and the style is loose and expressive with visible brushstrokes and outlines.
title: Station of the Cross No. 11: "Jesus is Nailed to the Cross"
